name: Smolensk
summary: Napoleon, hoping at last to bring the Russian armies to battle, closed on the walled city of Smolensk. Raevsky held its suburbs on the 16th while Bagration came up; on the 17th Ney, Davout and Poniatowski stormed the suburbs against Dokhturov's corps and the walls, but could not break into the city. That night the Russians fired it and withdrew across the Dnieper, and the French entered a burning ruin.

forces.name: Razout's Division
forces.summary: Ney's corps attacked the citadel and the western suburbs on the 16th and again on the 17th, without breaking in.
notes: After Nafziger's order of battle for the Grande Armée on 15 August, four days before the battle.
The 2nd Portuguese, of the Portuguese Legion, is shown as the list's Portuguese infantry.
The horse battery, without three cavalry regiments in the force, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Marchand's Württembergers
forces.summary: The Württembergers fought in Ney's assault on the suburbs on the 17th.
notes: Marchand, who had taken over from the Crown Prince, is the book's named commander.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the Grande Armée on 15 August, four days before the battle.
Nafziger's return gives each two-battalion regiment between 400 and 850 men, so every battalion is Small.
Two foot batteries, where the list allows one for this many battalions, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named General de Division Marchand, with his own rating.

Leclerc's brigade mixes a regimental battery with a section, and ten line battalions in a brigade is the list's limit; with the Mecklenburgers it has more. The horse battery, without three cavalry regiments in the force, shows as a historical departure.

forces.name: Kolubakin's Division
forces.summary: Raevsky's corps held the suburbs and the walls on the 16th against Ney's first attacks, buying time for Bagration's army to come up.
notes: Raevsky, the book's named commander, led this division's attack himself; Kolubakin commanded it.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the start of the campaign; losses since then aren't shown.
The story that Raevsky led the Smolensk regiment with his two sons beside him was a patriotic fiction he denied himself, though his elder son was with the army.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Borodino, three weeks later; the division was stronger at Smolensk.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Lieutenant-General Raevsky, with his own rating; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Neverovsky's 27th Division
forces.summary: Fresh from its fighting retreat at Krasnoi on the 14th, where its squares had held off Murat's cavalry for a day, it joined Raevsky in the defence of the suburbs on the 16th.
notes: After Nafziger's order of battle for Borodino. A new division of recruits; it had lost a quarter of its men at Krasnoi, and its guns there.
Nafziger gives it no artillery of its own; add a Light Battery if you like.
